\section[el gimnasio]{el gimnasio — the long form behind gym}

\label{lesson:ES-C412-gimnasio}



\begin{quote}
English shortens \textbf{gymnasium} to \textbf{gym}. Spanish keeps more of the old word: \textbf{el gimnasio}.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
Spanish \textbf{gimnasio} came through Latin \textbf{gymnasium} from Greek \textbf{gymnásion}, a place for exercise and training. English \textbf{gymnasium} is the same travelled word, and \textbf{gym} is its clipped form. Spanish spelling turns the learned \textbf{gy-} into \textbf{gi-}, pronounced with the strong Spanish \textbf{g} sound heard before \textbf{i}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: naming the place}]
The noun is masculine: \textbf{el gimnasio}, \textbf{un gimnasio}. Opening-hours signs often place the name first: \textbf{Gimnasio Atlas — abierto de 7 a 23 h}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{el gimnasio}
  \item \emph{un gimnasio}
  \item \emph{el gimnasio está abierto}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Gym? (\emph{El gimnasio}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/gimnasio}{DLE: gimnasio}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el deporte]{el deporte — recreation that became sport}

\label{lesson:ES-C412-deporte}



\begin{quote}
Recall the place for exercise: \textbf{el gimnasio}. What you may do there is \textbf{deporte}, sport.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{Deporte} belongs to an older \textbf{deportar} family that once meant recreation or amusement. English \textbf{sport} hides a useful cousin: it is the shortened form of \textbf{disport}, which came through French from the same Latin \textbf{deportāre} family. The histories narrowed toward organised physical activity.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: hacer deporte}]
Spanish commonly says \textbf{hacer deporte}, literally “to do sport,” for taking exercise. No article is needed in that general expression. Compare \textbf{el deporte es importante}, where the noun is the subject and keeps \textbf{el}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{el deporte}
  \item \emph{hacer deporte}
  \item \emph{hacer deporte en el gimnasio}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
To do sport? (\emph{Hacer deporte}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/deporte}{DLE: deporte}.
\end{tcolorbox}
